sections.title: Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
lecture_lines: A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes: Success or Failure.
The probability of success, p, must remain constant.
Think of flipping a coin: Heads is a success.
animations: Show a circle representing one Bernoulli trial, color #FFD700.
Color the circle half green (#32CD32) for Success, half red (#FF4500) for Failure.
Add labels 'S' (green) and 'F' (red) next to the halves.

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Conditions (BINS)
lecture_lines: Use BINS to identify a binomial experiment.
Binary outcomes and Independent trials are essential.
Number of trials is fixed and p is constant.
animations: Write the acronym BINS in #FFFFFF in the center.
Highlight BINS using a glowing effect in color #00CED1.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula
lecture_lines: The Binomial formula calculates success probability.
It uses combinations to arrange successes in n trials.
P(X=k) accounts for successes and failures.
n is the number of trials.
k is the number of successes.
animations: Write the formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).
Highlight C(n,k) with a surrounding box in #FF69B4.
Highlight p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) with a box in #7B68EE.
Animate the 'n' variable to scale up and blink.
Animate the 'k' variable to scale up and blink.

sections.title: Application: The Robot Scout
lecture_lines: Let's apply this to a Robot Scout.
Calculate the total probability for this outcome.
animations: Set mapping: n=5, k=4, p=0.7. Show these values in #FFFFFF.
Display 5 slots, color 4 of them green (#32CD32) and 1 red (#FF4500).
Draw a robot icon above the slots.
Move the robot icon across the slots to show 4 successes.
Display the final result: P(X=4) = 0.3601 in #FFD700.

sections.title: Summary & Visualization
lecture_lines: Distribution shape depends on n and p.
Changing p morphs the histogram shape.
animations: Draw a histogram for n=5, p=0.7 with bars labeled 0 to 5.
Animate the bars growing from zero to their probability values.
Highlight the total area under all bars in color #32CD32.
